meta: Is AI honest? Is it safe? With no right-or-wrong answer key, here's how people grade it: red teams play the bad guys to find holes, refusal tests, AI judges, and honesty checks.

muc.title: Grading what's hard to grade
muc.text: Last time, you wrote your own test for AI. But some things can't be graded with an answer key: is AI honest, is it safe?

muc.title: Red teams
muc.text: The first way: a red team. They play the bad guys and try to trick AI into doing things it shouldn't, so the holes get fixed early.

muc.title: Refusal tests
muc.text: The second way: thousands of dangerous requests, to see if AI knows to refuse. And the other way around: it shouldn't refuse normal questions for no reason.

muc.title: AI grading AI
muc.text: The third way: use an AI as the judge, grading answers against a written list of criteria. It grades thousands of answers fast, but AI judges make mistakes too, so people need to double-check.

muc.title: Knowing how to say "I'm not sure"
muc.text: What about honesty? Testers also ask questions AI can hardly know the answer to. A good AI will say "I'm not sure" instead of making up a confident answer.

muc.title: 5 parts in one picture
muc.text: Looking back at all 5 parts: standard tests, the cramming trap, the voting arena, your own test, and the things that are hard to grade.

muc.title: Will AI admit it doesn't know?
muc.text: Ask AI something you know the answer to for sure, like when the noodle shop on your corner opened. See whether it makes something up, or says "I'm not sure". Prefer an AI that can say it doesn't know.

muc.title: AI with many senses
muc.text: AI doesn't just read text anymore: it listens, talks, watches and even makes videos. How? See you in the new series: AI's senses.
